subject: Every string the arrange.regions surface exposes to AX in en-US
question: What labels does Logic show on arrange.regions in en-US, and on which elements?

reverify.expected: a census in en-US whose arrange.regions rows carry the same 12 distinct strings; a differing set means Logic's labels moved and every provenance citing this record wants re-reading
reverify.cost: ~1 min with Logic open on the fixture project in that locale

method: Read, never actuated. The menu bar and every menu were walked without opening them; the main window was walked to depth 8. Each element with any string became one row of the evidence file; rows were assigned to this surface by what their path or help text passes through, and rows no rule could place are counted in limits rather than filed.

strings: Add Tracks button. Add audio and software instrument tracks. Use tracks for recording, editing, and arranging regions.

Region starts at 1 bar  and ends at 2 bars , MIDI region. Contains MIDI note and controller events. Drag the middle to move, the lower edges to resize, and the upper-right edge to loop. Use the tools to perform other edits.
Workspace. The primary area for recording, editing, and arranging audio, MIDI, and Session Player regions, divided into different track types.

conclusion: On this host in en-US, arrange.regions exposes 11 elements carrying 12 distinct strings. Every string is in the evidence file verbatim, which is what lets a label variant cite this record: the guard requires the string to occur in the observations or evidence, and here it does or it does not.
limits: Navigation-free surfaces only: nothing behind a menu press or a button was opened, so this says nothing about the mixer, plug-in editors or the editors.
134 window rows matched no surface rule and are not filed under any record; they are in the evidence file and can be re-classified when a rule exists.
One project, one host, one build. A label that depends on project content — a track name, a region name — is a reading of this fixture, not of Logic.
